annotationRationale: The problem connects complex numbers with planar area. The main route uses rotation and similarity, while the alternative uses complex multiplication and coordinate area products; those route-specific concepts remain in their own methods.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate because the central task connects complex-plane points with quadrilateral area. No repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, the consecutive triangle areas are 2b and 8b, where b is the positive imaginary part. Thus 10b=15 gives b=3/2. The real part is sqrt(7)/2>1, so choice D is feasible and correct. No stem or choice contradiction; no question figure is supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. AoPS Solution 1 is retained through the similarity route. AoPS Solutions 2 and 3 and the LIVE calculation are consolidated into the Cartesian area route. The trigonometric shoelace expansion adds no distinct benefit beyond these two independently complete methods.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed complex-plane and coordinate-area concepts fit the question, and triangle area is appropriately supporting. The precise multiplication, polar-form, similarity and shoelace concepts appear in the relevant methods. Source-informed-original correctly distinguishes these explanations from official MAA adaptations.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate because the central task connects complex-plane points with quadrilateral area. No repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The hypotheses imply 0<theta<60 degrees, so the consecutive rays lie in order within the upper half-plane and the two triangles across OB do not overlap. Multiplication by z maps OUA to OAB and then OBC, multiplying each area by 4. Their areas are therefore 2b and 8b, giving b=3/2 with the stated feasible real part.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately credits AoPS 2024 AMC 12B Problem 12, Solution 1. The successive similarity argument is an original development of its triangle decomposition, rather than a sentence-by-sentence rewrite. The third-party basis is correctly labeled; no inherited shared-method credits are required.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The auxiliary point U makes the initial area b/2 transparent. The geometric effect of multiplication, area scaling, diagonal split and feasibility check are explained sufficiently without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four IDs fit: complex-plane geometry, polar multiplication and powers, similarity area ratios, and base-height triangle area. A separate rotation node is unnecessary because the polar node already describes the multiplication action.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for cnm_h098, cnm_272 and cnm_p148 fit the actual steps. Polar multiplication has no supplied CN alignment, which is an honest coverage gap.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: N-CN.B.4 and B.5 support polar representation and geometric multiplication; 6.G.A.1 supports triangle area. These uses do not establish all operations in those broader standards. The other complex-number links supply no evidence here of conjugates, quotients or complex midpoint calculations.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The immediate nodes precisely describe the written route. Only the relevant portions of the broader polar-power and similarity concepts are exercised.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The coordinates for z squared and z cubed are correct, as is u squared plus v squared=16. The two determinants simplify to 4b and 16b. Their opposite signs relative to OB justify the nonoverlapping triangle decomposition, yielding area 10b and the feasible answer b=3/2.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly identifies the LIVE calculation and AoPS Solution 3 for this exact question. Grouping the coordinates as u and v produces an independently written, shorter derivation. Both relevant third-party references are retained and the basis is accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The determinant is defined, its area and side-test meanings are stated, and both decisive simplifications are shown. The learner can reconstruct the calculation and understand why the areas are added.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Complex-plane interpretation, distributive complex multiplication and coordinate area products are all directly used. The sign test is an elementary consequence of the explained determinant and needs no additional catalog node.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for complex-plane geometry and complex multiplication fit. No CN link is supplied for shoelace.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: N-CN.A.2 supports the multiplication step; N-CN.B.4 contributes rectangular representation only. G-GPE.B.7 is appropriately partial for coordinate area. The other supplied links do not imply demonstrated conjugate, quotient, complex midpoint or factorization skills.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All three immediate nodes are precise and supported. The shoelace refinement supplies the essential area algorithm rather than relying on a broad coordinate topic.
